title: Latchkey shift handoff — overnight notes and pending actions
content:
TL;DR:
Overnight we saw a recurring tail-latency pattern affecting a subset of hosted API routes (chat streaming + long-context generations). Root symptom: unbounded KV-cache growth on a small percentage of Dedicated instances after large-batch uploads; memory thrash -> GC pauses -> token lag spikes (p95 -> 1.2s -> 4.8s in bursts). Incident is controlled, auto-fallbacks succeeded for most tenants, but two customers hit degraded streaming quality for ~18 minutes each.

What I saw (short):
- Alerts: routing-service latency alerts -> correlated with per-instance memory OOM warnings from the runtime.
- Affected surface: hosted-api routes that hit dedicated pools with mixed-model routing.
- Time window: recurring spikes between 02:12–02:30 and 03:06–03:25 UTC.
- Severity: Sev3 (customer-visible but no data loss).

Timeline (high level):
- 02:06 UTC: first p95 spike alerted (pager escalated to on-call SRE).
- 02:12 UTC: noticed memory growth on 3 Dedicated nodes (metrics: kv_cache_size increasing linearly).
- 02:18 UTC: temporarily cordoned node node-ded-42 to stop new work; downstream router rebalanced.
- 02:22 UTC: manual KV cache flush triggered via admin endpoint for node-ded-42; p95 recovered to 1.3s.
- 03:05 UTC: similar pattern on node-ded-47; automation did not trigger due to race condition in cache-watermark check.
- 03:12 UTC: fallback policy engaged; some clients routed to smaller-quantized model variant.
- 03:25 UTC: observed stabilization; monitoring group closed the immediate alert but left a persistent warning.

Actions taken during shift (notes):
- Containment:
  - cordon + drain on two nodes (node-ded-42, node-ded-47).
  - manual KV cache flush endpoint used: POST /admin/flush-cache?node=node-ded-42 (requires ops token).
  - temporary increase of cache-eviction aggressiveness on the routing config for the Dedicated pool (10% -> 35% eviction threshold) to reduce regeneration risk.
- Mitigation:
  - engaged fallback routing (canary to quantized-4k variant) for affected customer routes; client experience degraded gracefully.
  - raised autoscale minimum by 2 GPUs for period to reduce cold-start pressure.
- Observability & post-incident data capture:
  - uploaded heap snapshots from two nodes (S3: s3://redwood-inference-snapshots/latchkey/2026-11-25/).
  - exported timeline traces to Jaeger trace id root: trace: a1b2c3d4 (link in linked_artifacts).

Known impact / scope:
- Two paying customers experienced intermittent streaming fragmentation for ~18 minutes each; no token/account loss or data corruption.
- Internal SLA: minor impact (SLA-notify threshold not crossed), but this is customer-visible quality degradation.

Runbook gaps discovered (draft runbook notes):
- Existing KV-cache runbook covers "full memory OOM" but not the slow, linear cache growth pattern we observed. Need a new section: "progressive KV growth -> when to auto-flush vs. cordon".
- Automation race: cache-watermark-check job skips when multiple nodes report near-threshold at once. Add mutex/leader election or centralized throttle.
- Admin endpoints require ops-token; consider short-lived scoped tokens for runbook automation to avoid manual steps.

Follow-ups (owners + rough ETA):
- Diego A: implement conservative auto-flush trigger for KV-cache on Dedicated pools (PR + test) — ETA: 2026-11-30.
- Priya N: update routing config automation to increase eviction or backpressure earlier (config + rollout) — ETA: 2026-11-28.
- Zach Mills: write a runbook appendix "KV progressive-growth" and add playbook steps + exact admin commands (draft in Confluence) — ETA: 2026-11-27.
- Maya: correlate heap snapshots with model-architectural patterns and feed to runtime team; file follow-up issue in runtime repo — DONE (linked PR).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we prefer more aggressive eviction by default for Dedicated pools with mixed-tenancy? (ops input + product implication on quality).
- Should admin auto-flush be allowed without cordoning first? Risk vs. speed tradeoff.
- Add telemetry: per-request kv-cache-key-count metric (to distinguish warm vs. leak scenarios).

Incoming-shift quick checklist (what I want the next on-call to watch first 30m):
1) Watch the p95 latency dashboard for hosted-api > 1s sustained across 3+ minutes.
2) Alert channel: #sre-ops should reflect any repeated "kv_cache_size growth" logs — priority escalate if >2 nodes simultaneously increasing.
3) Confirm automation state for cache-watermark-check (cron status + last-run timestamp).
4) Verify no new heap-snapshot uploads pending; if there are, confirm S3 ingestion and TTL.
5) If repeat pattern appears, cordon the next suspect node immediately, flush cache, then drain.

Suppressed alerts / temporary silences we made: 
- Suppressed non-actionable GC chatter alerts between 02:00–04:00 UTC to avoid noise while we investigated. Make sure suppression window is removed at shift handoff.

Notes for on-call TL / handoff: 
- This is not a finished incident review — considered "operationally contained" but not resolved. We should plan a post-mortem if follow-ups aren't completed within one week or if incident recurs.
- Customer success: CS notified for affected customers; PR assigned to support: TEAM-1984. They will reach out if customers want incident summary.

Quick links: 
- Confluence draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/KV+Cache+Runbook (appendix 'progressive-growth' pending)
- Runtime repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/942
- Heap snapshots: s3://redwood-inference-snapshots/latchkey/2026-11-25/
- Jira: INC-7321, TEAM-1984

Hand-off acknowledgement: 
- Leaving this in the hands of the morning on-call. If you pick this up, ping me (Maya) in #sre-ops for any clarifying context.

Signed-off-by: Maya Chen (night shift)
